strategy.audienceName: Multi-promotion combat fans who plan their weekend around cards
painPoints: Fight schedules are scattered across promotions, broadcasters and timezones
Predictions made in group chats are forgotten by the time the decision lands
Disputed scorecards get argued from memory rather than from rounds
strategy.positioning: One app that holds every promotion's weekend, before the card and after it
strategy.targetAudienceSummary: Combat sports fans aged 18-34 who follow multiple promotions and argue about scorecards after every card
keyMessages: 12 events this weekend, all in one app
Predictions before the card, scorecards after it
toneGuidelines: Direct and factual; the number does the work
Fast in the first second, then let each screen be readable

creativeDirection.logline: Twelve events this weekend, and one app that already has all of them.
creativeDirection.visualDirection: Open on high-contrast gym footage with a hard push-in, then cut to app screens held long enough to read. Typography is heavy, uppercase and bottom-anchored inside the safe area. Accent rules mark the two screens that carry the numbers. Pacing tightens toward the end card.
creativeDirection.narrativeArc: A number that demands attention, the card that backs it up, the predictions that come before it, the scorecards that settle it, then the download.
referenceNotes: Hold each app screen at least a second and a half — a screen nobody can read is a wasted beat

hook.strategy: Lead on the count. Twelve is specific, checkable and larger than a viewer expects.

beats.description: Gym footage with a hard push-in while the count lands.
Ring-walk footage, taken from the second section of the clip rather than its opening.
The predictions screen drifting on a blurred backplate.
The scorecards screen, held still so the rounds are legible.
The designed brand card the end frame sits on.

factualConstraints: PRODUCT — Coverage: Combat Reviews covers every major combat-sports promotion in one app — MMA, boxing and kickboxing.
PRODUCT — Event details: Every card shows full fight order, start times in the viewer's own timezone, and broadcaster.
PRODUCT — Predictions: Users submit predictions before each card and see aggregated community picks per bout.
PRODUCT — Discussion: Round-by-round scorecards and post-fight discussion threads let fans settle disputed decisions with data.
PRODUCT — Price: The app is free to download and free to use; no subscription is required for event data or discussion.
EVENT — Events this weekend: 12 combat-sports events are scheduled across all covered promotions this weekend.
